subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning this as a single TypeScript module for a futuristic militarized truck, keeping it static without joints since vehicles don't need the articulation creatures would, which keeps the geometry simpler and safer in model space.

I'm sketching out dimensions: roughly 7m long, 2.8m wide, 3m tall with six wheels across three axles, a cab up front, an armored cargo bed with a turret, roof light bar, underglow, and decal textures for emblems and hazard stripes. I'm planning to use box and cylinder helpers along with an extrude for the angled hood profile, pulling in the clockwork kit for metal panels and glow effects while keeping colors gunmetal-dark for a militarized look.

Now I'm working out wheel placement and construction -- setting axle positions front and rear, sizing the tire and hub cylinders, and figuring out how to add lug nuts and tread detail around each wheel using small repeated cylinders positioned in a circular pattern.

I'm also designing the chassis frame rails, underbody skid plate, and axles, then moving on to building the cab as an extruded side profile defined by a z-y outline to get the hood and windshield shape right.

For the windshield, I'm giving it a dark glowing cyan tint and positioning it as a thin slanted box bridging the hood-back and roof-front points, computing the rotation angle needed to align the box's face with that slope.

Still placing panels... side windows next as thin boxes along the cab sides.

Now I'm detailing the cab front: a roof light bar, antennas, sensor dome, slanted glowing headlights, a vented grill texture, a heavy hazard-striped bumper wedge, a front plow blade, side skirts, and armor plates with emblem decals on the doors.

For the cargo section, I'm building an armored container box spanning the mid-chassis length with panelled paint, topped by a rotating turret with twin forward barrels, plus an angled rear missile rack of glowing-tipped tubes.

Still writing turret details...

I'm also planning the container's side panels with hazard decals, neon strip lines, and a faction emblem texture, positioned as mirrored planes on each side so the artwork reads correctly from both viewing angles.

Now I'm placing the rear elements: a hazard-striped back door, glowing red taillights, bumper and tow hitch, plus twin vertical exhaust stacks rising behind the cab with tapered glowing tips. I'm also working out clearance for cylindrical fuel tanks mounted between the front and rear axles, calculating their size and position so they fit without overlapping the wheels.

I'm now checking that the wheel arch fenders and wheels don't collide with the cab body, so I'm adjusting the cab's bottom height and wheel center spacing to resolve the overlap at the front.

Tires rest flat at floor level with 14-segment cylinders. I'm adding underglow strips in magenta beneath the sides, building out a cyberpunk palette of gunmetal, neon cyan, magenta, and warning yellow, plus a texture list covering hazard stripes, graffiti panels, emblems, grills, and plates, while sketching out the paint definitions for the hull.

I'm defining armor as a mottled olive military panel pattern with rivets, and the tires as dark near-black grain. Then I'm sketching out extra greebles: roof sensors, a glowing-tip antenna, searchlights, camera mirrors, a front winch, rear ladder, jerry cans, tow hooks, cage armor slats over the wheels, and skid plates.

Writing helper functions for boxes, cylinders, glow effects, and decals, then planning compact SVG textures -- a yellow/black hazard stripe pattern and a dark cyan-lined side panel design.

Now sketching the remaining decals: a monospace "NEO-ARMA 2077" logo with barcode and emblem, a hex shield emblem with "77", glowing grill slats, a license plate, and a HUD-style windshield texture with cyan readouts on dark teal.

I'm working out the windshield as a tilted plane with its own glow texture at moderate strength, plus extruding the cab, hood vents, side stripe decal, and a front bumper wedge profile using box and extrude geometries.

Now I'm placing hazard decal planes on the bumper's vertical face and refining the cab outline coordinates, adjusting where the cab front meets the bumper along the z-axis.

Working out the windshield slope between those two cab points, I calculate a slant angle near 28° with a normal vector pointing up and forward, and set the plane's center and size accordingly, lifting it slightly off the surface to avoid z-fighting.

Then I place headlight elements at the front face and extend the bumper geometry across the lower front region.

Now I'm sizing the grill plate centered between the headlights, then laying out the container body as a long box with a corner post framework, roof ribs, and side decal planes positioned symmetrically.

I'm adjusting the container's front edge so it overlaps the cab correctly, leaving a small gap filled by the chassis and exhaust stacks between the two sections, then placing a turret and missile rack on the container roof.

Now I'm laying out the missile pod geometry: a base box mounted on the roof with a 4x2 grid of tilted tubes, each tube getting a muzzle glow and inner dark disc at its end. I'm also starting the wheel-generating function, defining tire cylinders oriented along the x-axis.

Positioning tread blocks around the tire...

Adjusting tire radius slightly so the tread sits just above the floor without sinking in. I'm also laying out chassis details like driveshaft, axle diffs, and underglow strips, placing the glow boxes near the wheels at the sides of the chassis.

Now adding fuel tank cylinders near the rear with end caps, checking they don't collide with the underglow strips, then placing side mirrors with glowing screens on the cab.

I'm building out the roof details next -- a light bar with cyan and magenta glow segments, a sensor dome shaped from a partial sphere, antenna rods with glowing tips at the corners, and searchlight cylinders mounted on the A-pillars. Then I'm adding a front winch cylinder with a yellow cable ring and tow hooks, plus a spiked ram bar on the front bumper.

For the spikes I'm using cone geometries pointed forward instead of relying on bone-based placement, since that should work safely on an untagged root. For the rear I'm adding a bumper box, red glow taillight boxes, a hitch cylinder, ladder rods, and hazard/plate decals, and on the container sides I'm considering adding a few jerry cans, checking their placement height against the rear wheel positions so they don't collide.

Now I'm working out the vertical overlap between the side decal and the jerry cans — adjusting the decal's center height and thickness so it sits above the cans, then nudging the can positions slightly forward and down so they clear both the decal and the rear axle wheel fenders.

I'm also spacing out the wheel positions so the front, mid, and rear tires don't collide — checking the diameter against the gap between axles and shifting the rear wheel back slightly to leave a small clearance, then planning a dark skirt box between the axle zones for the lower armor plating.

Alongside that, I'm positioning the fuel tanks against the body, but their radius overlaps the skirt panel and the rail, so I'm nudging the tank x-position inward and thinning the skirt wall to avoid clipping.

Now I'm adding fenders over each wheel as thin dark boxes, plus a small mud flap behind the rear tires for detail, keeping these simple since the part count is already climbing toward roughly 230 objects, which feels like enough detail.

Now I'm setting up small typed helper functions for building parts—shortcuts for boxes and cylinders with position, direction, and color—plus a glow helper to add lighting intensity to specific pieces.

Still writing helpers...

Now I'm planning the exhaust cylinders, glowing tip rings, heat shield box, and front sensor pods before writing out the final export.
